ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a transmission line labeled Z0 = 100 Ω, and the load at the right end is formed by a resistor labeled R = 100 Ω and a capacitor labeled C = 10^-10/(2π) F connected in series between the upper and lower conductors. Reasoning: According to the image and the problem statement, the load is a series RC, and the transmission-line characteristic impedance Z0 = 100 Ω. The driving frequency f = 100 MHz = 10^8 Hz, so the angular frequency ω = 2π·10^8. The capacitance C = 10^-10/(2π) F, therefore ωC = (2π·10^8)(10^-10/(2π)) = 10^-2. The capacitive impedance ZC = 1/(jωC) = -j/(ωC) = -j100 Ω. The load impedance ZL = 100 - j100 Ω. The reflection coefficient ΓL = (ZL - Z0)/(ZL + Z0) = (100 - j100 - 100)/(100 - j100 + 100) = (-j100)/(200 - j100). Therefore F = |ΓL|^2 = 100^2/(200^2 + 100^2) = 10000/50000 = 0.2.
